summary: Trinity County, CA Shasta-Trinity NF tower: staffed by a volunteer in 2004, destroyed by wildfire in 2008 (Forest Lookouts says 2005); FFLOS-registered 2015; no source describes the site now.

facts.design: Tower with its deck 29 feet above the summit, reached by 41 stairs in a single steep flight (2004 visit report)
facts.status_note: Destroyed by wildfire; the 2008 Western Region report says lost in 2008 and Forest Lookouts says 2005; no source describes what remains

events.note: Woodpecker's beak pierced an automobile tire at the lookout house, per an October 8, 1938 item quoted by Forest Lookouts (Olean Times)
Staffed in 2004 by a volunteer; one of a dozen staffed lookouts on the Shasta-Trinity N.F. (visit report dated September 16, 2004)
Forest Lookouts says the lookout was overrun by the Lime Complex Fire on June 21, 2005 and the structure destroyed. Disputed: the 2008 Western Region report dates the loss to 2008
Western Region report says one lookout was lost to wildfire in 2008 and names Limedyke Lookout. The fire is not named in that report
Registered March 16, 2015 as FFLOS US 1590; nominated by Eliot Kalman

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Forest Lookouts dates the loss to June 21, 2005 (Lime Complex Fire). The 2008 Western Region report says one lookout was lost to wildfire in 2008 and names Limedyke. The record uses 2008 because it is the report's own date, but the disagreement is not settled and both are kept in events.

A May 2026 Forest Service release uses 'the Limedyke Mountain lookout' as a landmark in describing a fire. It does not say a structure stands. The record keeps status as gone because the sources that describe the loss say the structure was destroyed.

sources.title: Forest Service actively engaged in Limedyke Fire

notes_for_editor: No build date found in the sources read, so none is recorded. The 1938 woodpecker item is quoted over several lines on the Forest Lookouts page, and the 2005 burn date conflicts with the 2008 report. The firelookout.org list shows NHLR US 1321, CA 144 for Limedyke Mountain; the nhlr.org page was not in the cache (404), so no NHLR event is recorded. The 2026 Forest Service release uses the lookout's name as a place name only; check before publishing 'gone' without caveat. Access: only a 2004 road note exists, so access is omitted. The 2008 report does not name the fire.
